Read a multi-temporal stack for one Sentinel-2 band

Source: R/pixel-map.R
read_s2_band_stack.Rd

Stacks the cached `<band>.tif` files of several scenes into a single [terra::SpatRaster] with one layer per observation date. Layers are named by `as.character(obs_date)` and the corresponding [terra::time()] attribute is set, so callers can index by date.

Usage

read_s2_band_stack(cache_dir, scenes_df, band)

Arguments

cache_dir

Character(1). Same as [read_s2_band_raster()].

scenes_df

A `data.frame` with at minimum columns `scene_id` (character) and `obs_date` (Date, or coercible). Extra columns are ignored. Rows are re-ordered by `obs_date` internally. In practice this is the listing of scenes present in the COG cache directory for the zone.

band

Character(1). One of `"B04"`, `"B08"`, `"B12"`, `"B11"`.

Value

A multi-layer [terra::SpatRaster] in source CRS, with `names(out)` = `as.character(obs_date)` and `terra::time(out)` set to the dates of the surviving scenes. `NULL` when no scene could be opened.

Details

Missing scenes (no `<band>.tif` on disk) are skipped silently and reported via a **single aggregated warning** — never one warning per missing scene. Returns `NULL` if every scene is missing.

See also

[read_s2_band_raster()], [build_index_stack()] for computed NDVI / NBR layers, [extract_pixel_timeseries()].

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  cache <- "/proj/cache/layers/sentinel2"
  # scenes is a data.frame of (scene_id, obs_date); typically the
  # cache directory listing for the zone.
  scenes <- data.frame(
    scene_id = "S2A_MSIL2A_20250610T103031_R108_T31TGM",
    obs_date = as.Date("2025-06-10"))
  stack  <- read_s2_band_stack(cache, scenes, "B04")
  terra::time(stack)        # the dates as a vector
  terra::plot(stack[[1]])   # first scene
} # }
